destination.name: Wagga Wagga
destination.tagline: The largest inland city in New South Wales, on the Murrumbidgee River.
destination.description: Wagga Wagga is a city of about 57,000 on the Murrumbidgee River, midway between Sydney and Melbourne, and the Wiradjuri word is taken to mean 'the place where crows assemble in large numbers'. Charles Sturt was the first European to see the site, in 1829. The Botanic Gardens hold a rainforest gully, a succulent garden and a free zoo and aviary, and the Wiradjuri Walking Track circles much of the city for about 42 km. The city is also an army and air-force garrison town, with a base at Kapooka.
whyVisit: Stroll the Botanic Gardens rainforest gully
Ride the Willans Hill Miniature Railway

goodToKnow.title: Zoo and aviary days
goodToKnow.detail: The free zoo and aviary open Thursday to Monday, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

goodToKnow.title: Miniature railway Sundays
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage lists the Willans Hill Miniature Railway as running on the first and third Sunday of each month, about 2 dollars a ride; check before going.

goodToKnow.title: Maps at the visitor centre
goodToKnow.detail: Track maps are available at the Visitor Information Centre, 183 Tarcutta Street, open daily.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Autumn and spring, {months}, are the mild months for the riverside walking tracks and the gardens.
